question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>V</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mfenced><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi></math> represents the equation of state of some gases. Where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is the pressure, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is the volume, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> is the temperature and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>R</mi></math> are the constants. The physical quantity, which has dimensional formula as that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>a</mi></mfrac></math> , will be :

solution.text:
According to the principle of dimensional homogeneity, the dimensions of each  terms of a dimensional equation on both sides are the same.

So, dimension of b and V will be same,  b=V 

And dimension of aV2 and P will be same, aV2=P

From above two relations, we have ab2=P

∴b2a=1P=ML-1T-2-1

Thus, M-1L1T2  is the dimension of compressibility.
